deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen, new observatory, c. 1815–16. The previous page holds Aug. 1815 sun observations with an instrument that has an hour circle, plus a reading for the cross of the Jacobi tower. This page, 'Im Mittelpunkt der Sternwarte', is a horizon survey taken from the centre of the observatory, followed by a conversion of some landmarks to equatorial coordinates.

(A) Main table: landmarks around Göttingen. For each there is a horizontal-circle reading A and, for most, an altitude h.
- Landmarks: Warte bei Landwehr, Niederjesa, Roßdorf, a 6-tree group on the Hoher Hagen, Varmsen, Baum an der Chaussee, Hetgershausen, Johanniskirche (south and north spires), Rathaus, Jacobi, Clausberg, Albani, Jägers Gartenhaus, Gleichen (pointed and blunt), Geismar, Diemarden Warte, Hanstein, and 'Baum auf d. Hainb.' (a tree on the Hainberg; the transcription reads 'Heimb.').
- Geography fixes the zero point. Hanstein ≈ 359° (south), Hoher Hagen ≈ 60° (WSW), Hetgershausen ≈ 92.5° (W), Rathaus ≈ 177° (N), Gleichen ≈ 314° (SE), Hainberg ≈ 271° (E). So A is an azimuth counted from south through west, i.e. the astronomical azimuth.
- Below the table, at top right: 'Durchm. Landw. W. 9′9″' and 'Dim. W. 3′52″'. These are the apparent diameters of the two watch-towers (Landwehr, Diemarden), usable for distance estimates.

(B) 'Lage gegen den Aequator': hour angle t and polar distance p of seven terrestrial marks. The reading 'n^h d°m′s″' means t = 15n° + d°m′s″.
- The implicit transformation (mine, stated in modern form), with φ ≈ 51°31′48″ and A from south positive to west:
  - tan t = sin A / (cos A sin φ + tan h cos φ)
  - cos p = sin δ = sin φ sin h − cos φ cos h cos A
- Recomputation without refraction:
  - Hohehagen (A = 59°48′47″, h = 1°7′48″): t = 64°49.7′ against Gauss's 4^h4°50′37″ = 64°50′37″; p = 107°17.6′ against 107°17′43″.
  - Hetgershausen (A = 92°32′13″, h = 1°3′55″): t = 91°19.5′ against 91°18′3″; p = 87°35.3′ against 87°36′20″.
  - Clausberg (A = 220°25′23″, h = 2°19′40″): t ≈ 228°37′ against 15^h3°38′43″ = 228°38′43″; p ≈ 59°41′ against 59°40′11″.
  - Gleichen spitz (A = 314°15′1″, h = 1°33′38″): t = −51°48′46″ = 308°11′14″ and p ≈ 114°20′ (listed 114°22′7″). The listed '21^h 6°49′7″' agrees only if read as 21^h − 6°49′7″ = 308°10′53″, or as the mirrored 3^h6°49′7″. This presumably reflects the instrument-reading convention described on the previous page (12h added on the west side, opposite rule for negative polar distances).
  - Jacobi tower: computed t ≈ 186°20′, p ≈ 44°59′ against listed 12^h6°56′45″ and 44°54′10″. The previous page has 12^h6°48′15″, 44°56′5″ for the cross. The azimuth and altitude probably refer to a different point of the tower.
  - 'Jacobi SO' (polar distance 315°2′50″, i.e. −44°57′10″) appears to be taken in the reversed instrument position.
  - 'Baum a. H.': no altitude is listed, and the pair (t, p) cannot be reconciled with A = 270°44′19″ and any plausible small altitude. It probably comes from a different instrument position.
- So the equatorial values match the theodolite data to about 1′. That accuracy is expected, since the hour-angle/polar-distance readings were most likely read directly off an equatorially mounted instrument. The page compares and orients that instrument against the azimuths, i.e. determines its meridian and polar orientation using terrestrial marks.

(C) 'Mein Sextant': two pairs of readings, 119°32′5″ / 121°13′25″ and 142°33′40″ / 144°15′0″.
- Both pairs differ by the same 1°41′20″.
- The columns differ by 23°1′35″. The bottom-left entry is most likely 23.1.35, misread as 23.7.35.
- The bottom-right entry is (142°33′40″ + 144°15′0″)/4 = 71°42′10″ exactly, a mean half-angle. This looks like a sextant check or index-error comparison.
errors: Gleichen spitz hour angle as transcribed (21^h 6°49′7″ = 321°49′) disagrees with the azimuth/altitude by 13.6°. It agrees to about 20″ if read as 21^h − 6°49′7″ (equivalently mirrored 3^h 6°49′). This is a sign/reading convention, not a computational error.
Jacobi tower: listed t and p differ from values computed from A = 184°29′57″, h = 6°43′52″ by about 37′ and 5′. The points sighted probably differ (spire vs cross).
Baum a. H.: hour angle and polar distance are not reconcilable with azimuth 270°44′19″ for any plausible altitude. The source of the discrepancy is unclear (instrument reversal or a different point).
Residuals of about 1′ in the other marks are consistent with refraction neglected or instrument errors; not slips.

results.what: Horizon survey: azimuths (from south via west) and altitudes of Göttingen landmarks from the observatory centre
results.modern_name: theodolite azimuth/altitude observations of terrestrial marks

results.what: Conversion of terrestrial marks to hour angle and polar distance, used to orient an equatorial/hour-circle instrument

deep.surprise_reason: Purely observational log from the new Göttingen observatory: landmark azimuths and altitudes and their conversion to equatorial coordinates for instrument orientation. Routine practical astronomy, fully in line with Gauss's known activity in 1815–16.

checkable.asserts: 71°42′10″ is exactly one quarter of the sum of the two right-hand sextant readings (result 0)
Column difference is 23°1′35″ (result 0), so the '23.7.35' entry is likely 23.1.35

transcription_corrections: 'Baum auf d. Heimb.' is probably 'Baum auf d. Hainb.' (Hainberg, east of the observatory, consistent with azimuth ≈ 271°).
Sextant bottom-left '23. 7. 35' is most likely '23. 1. 35' (equals the column difference 23°1′35″).
'Dimardes Warte' = Diemarder Warte; 'Dim W.' = Diemarder Warte.
